I have enjoyed the open play and open world. You can explore and stumble upon things that will either kill you, bless you or reward you with items. There are many different npcs to discover, mobs that you can easily kill or come back to when you are stronger. The world is amazing! You can hear the ocean waves crash against the shore, the thunder of water against the cliffs, you can actually see whitecaps and waves make their way to the shore. I still have much to discover and do. You get a selection of classes to play that can be customized to fit your own style so there is no "cookie cutter" build. You get to choose how you want to play your given class and the weapons, skills etc. If you want to be a magic wielding rogue, it looks like it could be done. I am not sure how viable or survivable it would be but you have the option to do as you please. I really have no negative things to say about this game. I knew right then that this game was something beyond special. Elden Ring is a difficult game, especially for new-comers like me, who are new to the Souls-series of games, but that did not stop my endless amazement and sense of wonder every step I took. The environments, the bosses, the silent storytelling of the world around me was so.. unique. The more I played, the more I wanted to know, and I fell deep down the rabbit hole of this game's world. I will never forget the cinematic landscapes you see for each new area, the distant castle walls or giant golden trees. It is truly something you need to experience. The gameplay itself is quick and tight, the bosses pose interesting challenges that respect your time. Slaying a boss, especially the ones in the main story, feels like you really did something substantial, as often the world changes around you in their absence. You are only ever given one goal in Elden Ring that truly matters. Become the Elden Lord, no matter the cost.

This is one of the video games of all time. There is no doubt about that. Still, this is not a perfect 10/10 game for me and I will try to explain what I like and dislike about this game. This review is mostly spoiler free. This is my first Fromsoft game and some of the points may apply to all Fromsoft games I only played the first hour of DS3 so I don't know much about other FS titles. Things that I like: There is an insane amount of content to do. The exploration in early game feels really good and rewarding. You will meet/find something interesting and useful everywhere you go. There are 300+ weapons,60+ summons 150+ spells, 500+ armor pieces for you to find and make your build. The game feels like a true open world, just go and do whatever you like. You can add awesome skills to your weapon. You can change your weapons' scaling if it's a normal weapon. If you're running a dexterity build and want to wield that Berserk greatsword? You only need the base strength requirement then you can make the sword scale from dexterity by chaning it's affinity. You can wield very large weapons with one hand most other games will not let you do this. The game is somewhat difficult but you can complete everything, even if you are bad at the game, by using the tools game give you. Playing multiplayer is rewarded with a useful item which is difficult to farm in singleplayer. This is not an entirely sword & roll game, you can make all kinds of bombs, potions, throwing knifes, apply coating to your weapons to inflict elemental damage etc. The game has funny things in it like a big jar dude and funny armors Level and World design is astonishing. Environmental storytelling is very strong. You can tell a lot about what happened in an area just by looking. You can play this game as hack&slash game or survival horror game all depends on your build. [spoiler] bro becomes a meteor [/spoiler] Things that I dislike: Repeating bosses. Some bosses will appear 10+ times. I know it is very difficult to fill a map this big with unique bosses but if you care about it you should know this before. They could have made the world smaller and nobody would complain. Dungeons all feel samey, same enemies with same layoutat the end there will be a the same boss room. The quest system is bad. If you're playing this blind without looking stuff online, chances are, you are going to miss a good portion of the game. NPC quests are literally you talk to a guy then he teleports to a random location and you talk to him again and repeat. To unlock 2 entire endgame areas you need 2 items, one drops from a boss and the other one is at a totally random location where you have to hit a random pot to get it. In the endgame exploration is meh, you do some platforming & fighting and find an item, "upgrade material 6" but you can buy the same thing infinitely for a small price at that point. Game performance is bad, the game runs on less frames than some other open world rpg with similar graphics. After you made it into endgame the difficulty spikes up considerably. Not only the bosses but normal mobs will 1-2 shot you unless you have very high health and heavy armor then maybe 2-4 hits. There are normal enemies that are harder to kill than most of the bosses. The difficulty is unbalanced. There is a boss type of enemy guarding the main boss arena door. He is harder to defeat than the real boss inside. He is on horseback but you can't use your horse, no summons, nowhere to hide from his ranged attacks. He also has more health & hits harder and you can't land a crit attack on him. Certain enemies will punish you for healing, the moment you drink your health potion they will launch a long range attack to interrupt you. People call it input reading and I think it is pure BS. Some fights have a rythm and flow, you can dodge attacks intutively. Some other fights have delayed attacks to trick you. The dude holds his sword up in the air for 5 seconds and you wait for it. I don't think this is fun and does not fit into the context of "melee fighting". A few enemies spawn fires on ground, when you touch it the fire will kill you instantly. This doesn't make sense when you touch fire it sets you on fire then you take damage slowly. You fight very large enemies to die attacks you can't even see since you're just attacking his foot and tickling down his health. Good and interesting characters with very little screentime. Enemies and regions have static level. You are over or under leveled most of the time. You will discover a castle to insta kill the boss inside since you leveled up too much Coop mode is limited, the game limits you in an area with the goal of beating the area boss. You will be sent back to your world after defeating the area boss. There are very useful craftable items which require collectibles that are limited in the world or very tedious to grind. Some aspects of the game are similar to MMORPGs where you farm item b so you can farm item a. Input Buffering, if you press roll 2 times quickly you will roll again after done rolling. This input system is almost never useful it is only there to punish you for spamming buttons. Story is average, there are interesting side quests and lore elements but the main story of the game is you wake up and kill everything. If you look at it there is no story in the game, only a very small number of events happen in your playthrough. A normal playthorugh is literally "go kill the main boss", "ok i made it to the main boss but the door is locked", "go kill 10 other bosses to unlock the door", "kill the main boss". The game is not story driven but lore driven. One of the questline and ending is confirmed to be mistranslated (the ending turns out to have a complete opposite meaning) from the original Japanese script in to English. This raise the question; how much of this game is translated accurately? Second phase of the final boss is the worst type of video game boss. That one boss hits you once and runs 10km away and you chase him the entire figth kind of boss. Many people say the figth was designed with your horse in mind but they forgot to enable it. The game has a system where if a merchant NPC dies you will obtain their shop item and their shop will be available in the hub world. At first this seems like the devs don't want you to miss anything in the game but this is a total scam. You can still miss items.

As many have said, it's quite an adventure and definitely worth playing for souls fans and anyone who likes a true action rpg. It's certainly not a 10/10, but not for lack of content. In fact, the game would've benefited from a few features/areas being cut. There is easily a full game's worth of unique content here, looking at the scale of the world, the number of areas, weapons/spells, and bosses. However, a lot of the content is repeated to the extent that the game is the scope of 2 or 3 full games. So instead of a normal-sized game where everything is unique and has a purpose, the game has a lot of re-used content and is a bit bloated. So after the 80-ish hour mark, the scope of the game actually works against itself, in my opinion. The first 40 or 50 hours are sheer bliss and rival my best experiences playing almost any other game, but it falls off bit by bit as you explore more of the worlds areas, finding nearly identical catacombs or caves, consumables that just have a different coat of paint, the same ruined churches/enemies, and mini bosses that are re-used over and over with slight alterations or coupled with other enemies for increased challenge. enemy and item placement is generally fantastic, and i always felt like the developers were right next to me, watching me play and placing everything by hand. So even when the content is re-used, exploring is still pretty engaging because there are very few empty dead ends. The overall narrative is intriguing, but any actual explanation of the characters/world/who you are/etc are pushed so far to the sidelines that my biggest bit of positive feedback on this front is that it doesn't get in the way of the experience. And I'm absolutely forced to mention that characters' names are just unbearably similar, I really have no idea what they were thinking here. They took so many liberties with the narrative that they seem to have said to themselves "it's probably better if it just doesn't make any sense and leaves the world in a state of mystery." I'm not sure I agree. I'm tempted to say that the core systems (that is, the combat, menus, and upgrades) are excellent, but honestly there are some big holes in the experience that I can't overlook. It's difficult to summarize, but certain aspects of the game are too obscure considering how critical they are to the whole of the experience. Magic is a great example, as summons, incantations, and sorcery and more are all handled differently and are obscure enough that I wouldn't blame players for skipping most of these mechanics entirely. Sorcery in particular involves finding a specific NPC in the world that is hidden in a copy-paste hole in the ground that could EASILY be overlooked given the size of the world. Summons are granted through the use of an item which is obtained through an NPC that only appears during one part of the game's day/night cycle (which influences very few other parts of the game afaik), and incantations require equipping and using "seals," which is not very obvious. All these things and more are likely explained/hinted at early in the experience but given how much is thrown at you, it's impossible for all of it to stick. Although it's sort of magical how every game mechanic is veiled in an in-world name (Runes = XP, Ashes of War = special skills for weapons, "Tears" are health flask upgrades, etc), this makes for a very, very laborious process of trying to figure out if an item is even important or not. Speaking of importance, consumables make up a lot of the loot in the game, and in a game where the biggest challenges is bosses which will regain all their health when you die, consumables seem meaningless to me. My first 5 attempts at the more difficult bosses will just be learning attack patterns. Crafting is pointless because you only craft one-time-use consumables which I've already stated that I find useless. Crafting should've been excluded entirely from the game but I'd guess it was left in as an additional incentive to explore/revisit ares of the map. 'Questing' is executed poorly enough to be a considerable net negative on the experience. NPCs appear in different places seemingly at random and the world is simply too big for this too be acceptable, especially without a questlog of some sort. There are a few types of loot that I was always happy to find: Smithing Stones (used to upgrade weapons), Talismans (usually stat modifiers that can be easily swapped out to sort of re-spec your character on the fly), armaments/armor, and Runes. Every other bit of loot was almost always pointless and I would shrug and say to myself, "well, exploring and killing enemies is its own reward. Talismans are great and maybe one of my favorite systems in the game. XP and weapons/gear are pretty straightforward, as loot at least. Smithing Stones, however, change the game in an important way that I love and hate, and ultimately wish was different. Upgrading weapons means that you can stick to certain weapons long after they should be obsolete, which is good in that you can use your favorite weapons for most of the playthrough, but because some weapons are so much better in terms of DPS than others, i found myself using only 3 different weapons during 90% or more of my 160 hours. There are an insane number of interesting weapons, so it's a shame that I never saw a path to success by trying lots of different ones. Smithing stones are also a pain-point in that finding a specific 'level' of stone is required to upgrade each stage of the weapons' power. what this means, is that at times, A level 7 smithing stone may be more valuable than an 8 or 9, simply because your weapon's upgrade is gated at each level and you might have run out of 7's. Still, smithing stones are always an exciting find and make exploring fun. I'm not going to say much about the visuals; in terms of asthetics the game is an easy 10/10. It's truly a breathtaking game and I can't count how many times I said to myself during my playtime "wow. I've never seen anything like that before." Audio is great, OST is pretty spectacular and the music always matches the tone of the situation it accompanies. Last thing I want to cover is bosses, which are sort of a mixed bag. I'm not surprised this is a big point of contention for the community; some of them are very fun once you get the hang of their moveset, while others are just simply too cruel and unfair to be enjoyable or satisfying once you've conquered them. Almost every boss requires carefully timed dodges and a mastery of stamina management and character building. That's fine. What really isn't fine is bosses reading player inputs to trigger attacks the exact moment you do something, bosses that track perfectly, forcing dodge rolls instead of just clever footwork, absurdly long combos, Multiple boss phases, incorrect or very sloppy hit boxes and one hit kills. A boss could have one or two of the above and still be a fair fight, but I'd say the majority of the main bosses (and quite a few of the minibosses) have most or all of those features. I'm not saying any of the bosses aren't possible with time and effort, I'm saying a lot of them aren't very fun. Given the various types of character builds, the length of the game, and the fact that co-op is potentially part of the experience, I think the devs erred on the side of making bosses too overpowered, unfair, or tedious. If fighting bosses was less common I might give this a pass, but such a large percent of my playtime was spent in boss encounters (often fighting a new boss immediately after beating a previous one), that I really just got tired of the experience and wanted it to end. Now, this review has mostly focused on the negative features of the game, but I think the positives more than make up for it. This is really a breathtaking epic experience that, despite being flawed, is definitely worth a recommendation. Game of the Year? Maybe. 10/10? nope.

Don't let the difficulty hype discourage you. This is just a common RPG game minus the quest markers and journals, quick saves, and tutorials. Like any other RPG, you'll die if you play it like an action FPS. Pay attention to your surroundings and you'll do fine. There is tons of info online to get you going if you want to start the game off easy or if you need more info about anything in the game. I didn't feel like any of the game mechanics were poorly implemented or frustrating, it actually plays very well, at least with a gamepad. I fought all of the optional story or shard bearer bosses and only one of them was a major pain. I didn't 100% the game, but completed various dungeons, cleared the underground areas, and explored much of the overworld area; completed all that in 120 hours. Never had the game crash or consistently stutter, its main issue is that it is single-threaded. It will try to use all of one CPU core, so it seems like it might briefly lock if something else wants to use that CPU core, but that might have happened 3-4 times for me. I played with an i7-9700K + RTX3090 and the game ran smooth 99.999% of the time. The game may briefly stutter after updating video drivers, I assume it's compiling shaders, but that seems to go away within a minute. From is basically the Japanese version of Bethesda, they've been building on the same engine for an eternity, stamping out cookie-cutter games running on newer iterations of that engine, so don't expect an audio/visual masterpiece. The art design looks good, but isn't cutting edge, and the audio is alright, but don't expect a fabulous hi-fi experience. The game world is interesting and gameplay is fun.

After almost a year with this game, after 450hrs or so playing this game on and off, completing all the achievements, playing with multiple characters, with my friends, dabbling in pvp and invasions, and slight bit of modding. I can proudly say it was worth the hype. I'll assume people familiar and those who have played previous FromSoft titles have already played this so for those WHO ARE UNFAMILIAR with the souls series and are wondering if it is worth playing. It is. I played this with two friends who have never played a soulsborne game in their life and we thoroughly enjoyed it. There are a few caveats for a new player but I'll base this both on my personal experience and my friend's opinions on our journey. Here are some things to consider. * I'll preface what you need to consider before buying the game with this. This is a long game. You will have to devote a lot of hours into this game. Mind you, not just at one sitting but it will be a while to finish a new game. It can go from 60~150hrs for a first playthrough depending on how much you want to explore and how good you are at the game. So consider that this isn't an over the weekend type of game and if you are fine with that, then let's move on. * This is an action-rpg, you will have to learn the mechanics of the game and be somewhat adept to it. That goes for both understanding the role-playing aspects and the technical aspects of playing the game. Mashing 1 button with your starting gear can work for a while but without learning how to upgrade, using talisman's, boss mechanics, enemy and level layouts, you're gonna have a bad time. FromSoft's level design is impeccable and you'll slowly pick all of this up intuitively if you pay attention to what the game tells you. * There is no difficulty slider, there is one difficulty and that's it. Your playthrough's difficulty will depend on your play-style and how much you want to delve into the numerous in-game mechanics of the game. There is nothing wrong with asking for help, looking for help, and searching for help. Whether it be youtube, the wiki, reddit, or online players, it's fine as long as you're enjoying. * Co-op is super fun but is also annoying (sometimes). Traditional in-out multiplayer is not what Elden Ring offers, while I am familiar with Dark Souls co-op, invasions, and pvp, my friends were not. It takes about 3-5 sessions with friends before they'll get used to it and stop complaining. There are also invasions where the most fun and frustration was had. Pretending to be chairs and watching an invader get confused then corner themselves was fun but you'll also get the occasional god who can just destroy you as you run towards a boss. So, in conclusion, it's fun, convoluted, frustrating and the most unique multiplayer experience we had. * Have fun. This is a challenging game, but a lot of enjoyment can stem from that challenge. IT IS NOT FOR EVERYONE. Anyone can play it but that does not mean they will enjoy it. If you feel that you won't enjoy the game, that's fine, it doesn't mean you are a lesser gamer for it. You can revisit the thought of playing someday. However, if you have been craving for a different experience from your typical open-world, map marker, get into the top of the tower and unlock the map game, then this might be a refreshing and even life changing experience for you. The game's approuch to open-world deisgn is phenominal. Interconnected zones that are inhabited with such unique enemies and are leveled in a way that doesn't seem unfair (at least not at the first half of the game). These zones intuitively show you where to go and how to get into them. So enjoy the feeling of exploring the beatiful world created by Miyazaki and his team. And if you do choose to buy this game, welcome fellow Tarnished, into The Lands Between. Serious Critique Time: (Here I put some of the things I observed that can I found viable for discussion) * Performance - during the first week, the performance was abbysmal and while it got better over time, I am still getting dips from certain areas. I'm sure this won't happen but implementing DLSS or FSR into the game may help some or even in their future games. * 60 FPS cap - I know, it's for balancing with multiplayer. I personally got my ass whooped by a dude who kept stuttering while running and attacking. This is apparently caused by unlocking framerate. I'm unsure if it's the engine, netcode, or whatever reason but other multiplayer games have found a workaround for this so maybe in the next game, it would help if they could allow us to remove the 60fps cap since they have made a push for more multiplayer. * Boss and enemy variety - I always found it a strange critique due to how many different enemy and boss designs are in the game. There is an absurd ammount of unique enemies and bosses in the game as compared to other open-world titles. Even the repeat enemies for the later half of the game are unique enough for me to not find it annoying, however, what I do find annoying is the ammount of the damage they do. * End-game difficulty spike - I like the soul's challenge but by god does it suddenly kicks you in the balls then start spitting at you as you get up. Maybe I can say it wasn't that hard because my first time through the game I did not notice it but playing it again with friends suddenly made me realize how ridiculous the damage end-game areas can do to you, especially with multiplayer scaling. I don't know why I did not feel this in my first playthrough but with subsequent playthroughs it did seem unfair in a bad way. Overall, these are nitpicks that I found after multiple playthroughs. I played this game on release and finished it after a month. This game is an experience and will leave you amazed and overwhelmed with how wonderful and terrifying the world is. I just can't wait to see what's next for us tarnished. Please Miyazaki, give us the DLC.

I've been an avid action rpg player since I was a kid, starting with Phantasy Star Online on the Dreamcast. In 2022 and 2023 I played a lot of Splatoon 3, Monster Hunter Rise, and am more recently Playing Risk of Rain 2, Valheim, and Deep Rock Galactic. All of these games I listed have superb combat and very fitting combat. They feel good, they're fun, and I find all of these games to control in an enjoyable way. By that, I mean that they have excellent gameplay. Elden Ring's gameplay feel and loop are very poor. The controls and gameplay itself have offered me the least fun that I have ever had in an action rpg game. Now, before you begin harassing me in claims that I just don't like "difficult" games, I found that Elden Ring is one of the least punishing action rpgs I have ever played. If you are spending your runes, as you should, then death in this game is literally not a problem at all and there is no reason to fear dying. So punishing is definitely not a term I would use. "Difficult" is somewhat of a subjective term, but what I am assuming players mean by "difficult" in this context is not "difficult", but actually tedious. You really only have about 3 things that you might do: One is to dodge, dodge, dodge, and of course to dodge again and again. The main gameplay loop is to continually dodge poor optimized, in terms of time, attacks. The key to not getting hit is to time your dodge, but if you play this game or watch gameplay, there are so many times when you expect to get hit but don't or expect not to get hit but do. Ultimately, this leads to nothing more than spamming the dodge button like a madman as a go around to this issue. And that ultimately leads to boring gameplay. The second thing you might do is attack. Attacks are done on a controller using the R1 and R2 triggers. The R2 trigger gives you a kind of charge attack or a slower but heavier hit. However, as we talked about timing issues, R2 is just far too impractical to even bother using with a basic melee weapon. It is better to get your poke in with an R1 then run, or rather, to continue your dodge-athon. Which leads me into explaining why this is so terribly boring. You are spending most time avoiding combat and being disengaged for one, but more importantly, there isn't a lot of action coming from the player, or combos, or effects that might compromise the opponent, or disable them, or lead to giving the player some kind of advantage due to their fight strategy and so forth. The action part of the action combat is the player running and evading a barrage of attacks or projectiles from an enemy combatant. Sure there are spells and you can summon pets or something to spice things up, but if you want to play, or rather, engage in combat, your access to participate in the process of action within this ACTION rpg are incredibly limited. The third main thing that might comprise your gameplay is using items, which would be a bomb, or a heal potion, or mana potion, whatever you are carrying with you. These potions are your main source of healing or mana rejuvenation and you will be using them a lot to continue your combat participation. However, there is a very very big problem with this system. You want to make sure that you have the item you may need to use on the fly as your selected item because you do not want to have to change active items during combat, as the joystick that controls your sprite is separate from the joystick to change items, which would be your d-pad. Now, strategically this adds excitement into what would be otherwise very boring gameplay, due to the strategy of selecting items before engaging or running away so you can switch to your mana potion to continue casting spells, or whatever, but the real problem here is that you are literally taking control off of your character in order to access your items. The switching of items requires a letting go of control of your character and creates a back and forth of engagement and disengagement. Monster Hunter does this too with their item system, but in the case of Monster Hunter it has very little effect on your ability to continue engagement in the battle. You can wire bug and dive back in. In Elden Ring you dodge like a madman, get far far away, then switch items or heal or whatever, then dodge dodge your way back in. It's simply tedious and boring and this is because your sprite completely lacks mobility. And, Monster Hunter does not make you feel like you are giving up control of your character to access items. In sum, there are better games out there. The popularity of this game just goes to show that it is not quality that people desire but to be a part of the popular. The best I could give this game is a 7/10 and even that 7 seems overly generous. The combat is boring, does not feel rewarding, makes you feel gimped and weak (not in a positive way), discourages engagement, and is severely lacking in complexity or technique. Defeating an enemy gives you no satisfaction due to anything you have done and simply leaves you with an empty feeling of relief. I would not recommend this game to anyone.

Getting to NG+5 on the non steam version, I can definitely say I've played a lot more than my steam hours states. There are things done RIGHT: The Open World is intruiging, Combat feels great, It runs fantastic, The World looks GORGEOUS, There are some areas inside the Open World that are legitimately INSANE, The Mobs, Bosses and NPCs are well desgined, The Sounddesign is good and weapons, attacks, etc all are fantastic However this can't carry the negatives I found with this game: Feeling Lost: I know it's a meme, but hear me out. I literally SKIPPED the tutorial by accident. I walk here: "oh the enemies are too hard, you need to go elsewhere" my friends tell me. Well so I did. I walk there: Now I'm oneshotting everything since I was MEANT to go there much earlier. That is no fun. How should I know which level of "hard but fair" is acceptable? No idea. I wanted to play this game blind, but I literally could not - I would've quit the game 5 hours into it if I had no friends to teach me. I frequently find myself asking: "can I fight this one?", "Am I supposed to be here?", or "How do I find X?"."Go find out for yourself!" say my friends. "The game tells you when you are not meant to be here", they say. This is where I don't agree: No guidence at all lets me feel lost, clueless, I had no idea on how to do basic things, sometimes I'm overlevelled, sometimes I'm underlevelled. Elden Ring, for the love of god, is HORRIBLE at communicating information to the player. I know you all are down to BASH hand-holding the player, but SOME guidence should be given. And NO, The questlines and storylines all don't make sense and are rather missleading, sometimes leading you to areas you most certainly shouldn't be, to be fully honest. Being Open World makes this problem 10x more apparent. Let's talk more about that. Variety: Going Open-World has it's problems. I frequently find myself uninterested in the exact same Dungeons, Bosses, Boss-Rooms, Enemies. The entire copy-paste of some sections had me feeling disappointed. This hits much harder because I know they CAN do better. Some of the most breathtaking areas I've ever experienced are in this game. But you can't fully build the Open World on these areas, right? Well you just have to look at other Souls games to recognize that this is very possible. A lot of bosses also get reused or become normal Mobs - which apparently is normal? I'm not getting exited anymore when seeing (most) BOSSES. Think about that. Meta is also a big part of Variety. I personally have no idea about this stuff tbh, but I frequently heard about meta builds being broken or nessassary to defeat harder bosses, PVP-builds all being the same, etc. This hurts the integrity and one of the best aspects of the game: play however you want. Point proven: Elon Musk literally got flamed and people wrote articles about him for using an "off-meta" build. wtf? I'm HEAVILY discouraged of doing so, because X is most broken, ,Y is nessassary to beat stuff or, going to my next point, I levelled Z. Limitation: Some limitation is very good and welcomed. However I REALLY dislike how weapons and Arts are Stat-Locked. How come I defeat the X-Dungeon or boss, wasting hard-earned Stone-Keys to play them, just to come out with a lackluster experience and a weapon I can't use? This feels genuinely HORRIBLE. Yes, I've been told I can respec, but 1) I have literally no idea how (feeling lost), and 2) I can do this only a limited amount of times. And no, I don't want to REPLAY the entirety of Elden Ring because, and this is the singular reason my friends replay this game, I want to try a new build. This seems INSANE to me. It's unfair: Some Bosses and Mobs felt very unfun to play against (don't get me started about this invisible dude). I don't really want to waste 6 hours for the TUTORIAL BOSS. So what did my friends do? (this was one of the biggest mistakes I've done); we cheesed a Mob way beyond my league (but accessible for some reason; that doesn't make sense), giving me an INSANE amount of Levels. I've become overlevelled to the point where I still first-try bosses 40 hours into it. As a Newbie to Souls-Games. That doesn't feel right nor fun. Hearing that the lategame gets worse, with frequently more unfair enemies, I feel very discouraged to go on. I came into Elden Ring and wanted a "Hard but Fair" game, but this couldn't be further from what I've experienced. Story: I literally have no Idea why I play this game on a story-perspective. I know I want to be this Elden Lord, go to that Tree or whatever, but that's about it. The only reason I kept playing is because I want to find special places, see something I didn't see before. It comes down to everything feeling VERY confusing. I have this quest where I needed to go down a well to find some NPC. The Well-part was rather easy, but down there and without guidence by my friends I would've probably searched for a bit - then I found him and CAN'T EVEN PROCEED this questline. "The next part is out of my reach for some time" my friends tell me, seeing no problem with that. Multiplayer: Multiplayer was a mistake. It's frequently laggy, It takes AGES to play together, it's very limited and there are exploits that feel like straight up cheating. This shouldn't be the way you play this game imo. PVP is also very unfun, running into the same builds a lot of times ("YO It's another Guts-Build"- my friends shout in exitement). This is a personal point to be fair, but let it be mentioned here. This game is far better enjoyed in Single Player. This is where I stand: I intentionally didn't go deep into the positives to prove my point but trust me: This game got GREAT things going for it. That's why I'll keep playing after all. It's far better than many Triple A titles (which is not hard to be fair). I first thought Souls-Games are just not my type of game, but I've disproven that by liking other souls-games I've played recently. I've truely thought I'm a noob, that the game is too hard because... well... I'm too bad. But that wasn't true aswell. I've finally stopped giving it the benefit of the doubt, "breaking my silence" one might say, and saw it for what is it: A great game with huge deal-breakers and impossible problems to solve. It's near impossible to play this game without any help, it lacks direction, multiplayer is bad, the story is a confusing mess, the Open World hurts the game more than it does good. This game is far from being the masterpiece people praise it to be. To my friends: Tut mir Leid Alex und Christian, ich hab euch häufig getriggered, aber Elden Ring hat zu viele Probleme, welche mir den Spaß richtig oft rauben. :(

After a long hiatus due a hand injury, I've finally finished it and it's one of those gems that I feel like has impacted me on almost a spiritual level so I wanted to just leave a review. It's GOTY for a reason. That being said, expect a little bit of jankiness, but get ready for a huge world to get lost in. Lots of challenges to tackle in your own way. Beautiful screenshot worthy vistas. Frustrating and scary moments. Jaw dropping enemy designs. Tons of weapons, spells, armor to try out. Take the time to interact with the characters and read item descriptions to give you an idea of the shattered world your character has arrived in, there's a lot more than meets the eye. I have a few gripes, namely that there are so many weapons and items but there is a hard limit on how many times you can re-spec your character, it limits experimentation and creativity. The item upgrading system, well, let's be real, a handful of systems are a bit convoluted too. But don't let that stop you. I recommend a blind experience but look up things when you need to because the game doesn't explain things very well, specially if you're new to souls games. Don't be afraid to try it. The game at it's core is about perseverance. It's a souls game, it's brutal. Don't give up. Some of the bosses took me days to learn and beat, but the feeling of overcoming a challenge like that is just bliss. Take breaks if you need to, explore different areas and try various methods to beat the bosses. Elden Ring has so many more ways to play the game than the older souls games and to make it easier on yourself if you want to by using summons or summoning help. Or you can challenge yourself and self impose your own rules. That's the beauty of it.

Ill be honest. I've never really ever liked single player games. I've tried the whole lot of them, none of them I ever really liked or for any matter, got into at all. It took me a long time of debating on this one after seeing all the praise it got, but as you can see, i'm here. Some people call this game misdirected, or maybe even "too hard" But I call it the closest thing you can get to perfection in a video game. Here's why: Elden Ring teaches you about discipline, it teaches you about commitment, and it also teaches you about freedom. There is a common misconception behind this game, some people say its too cryptic to know where your going. Which is the complete opposite of why this game absolutely excels. Elden Ring gives you absolute and total control of where you want your character to go in the open world it provided. You will rarely find any aspects of the game that limit you to where they want you to go. Making it the absolute holy grail of open worlds. Elden Ring will help you with real life scenarios and issues, This game will ultimately help to train you to achieve your goals, because throughout playing this game not only to you have to manage your anger (as did I) but you have to push through when you find a certain aspect difficult. Which is why the intense difficulty of the game makes it different and refreshing from every other game currently out there. The Story is stunning, as well as the visuals. Cutscenes are almost as if not more immersive than a film. You will find yourself immersed in the world of Elden Ring immediately. Even if you don't consider yourself a video game type of guy, or a single player type of guy, I recommend you try this game out. Take my word for it, its great.

I want to first say that I don't want to recommend, or not recommend this game. For some it will be phenomenal, while for others it will be terrible, and that is just a fact. It's a shame I am forced to select one or the other. Since the game is so hyped in one direction, recommended, I guess I will do the opposite in the spirit of balance. I don't get the appeal of games like this. They are TOO hard to enjoy. If you want the exploration that is expected in an RPG, you will find it here, but every bat can kill you unless you also enjoy mastering combat. I don't want to do anything more than press a button to swing a sword, or cast a spell, and perhaps dodge or block like you do in GW2. If you are like me then I recommend you avoid this game regardless of the rave reviews. I played this game much longer than I expected because I spent $60 on it, but here are the issues as I see them: Pros: 1. Exploration of the open world is really second to none. This is a fantastic open world with a mystery and excitement to it akin to Everquest 1 when it first released. 2. The variety of mobs is fairly high 3. The graphics and ambient sounds are well done 4. The first act of the game, when mobs are not ridiculous and everything is new, is simply the best experience I have had in years. Most reviews go on and on about this same thing so I won't reiterate it here. What most reviews don't mention are the negatives, and there are negatives for many types of players despite the thousands of positive reviews. Cons: 1. Tedious: if you die you lose all runes which are collected like gold would be in most games, but are also the only way to level; you get one shot to pick them up again, but if you die they are gone for good along with every single bit of progress you have made in earning them. Also, when you die ALL previously killed mobs respawn and you have to fight your way back through them. I despise repeating things, and this game is designed to kill you over and over so you will spend a lot of time repeating stuff. 2. There is no real sense of getting more powerful. Sure there are mobs you eventually become stronger than, but you are always just a few unfortunate hits and stuns away from death no matter your level, experience, or gear. 3. There is no way to adjust difficulty, so if you become mentally weary of the fights and just want to explore the world and story on a slighty lower intensity, you can forget it. 4. After reaching the capital you will notice that mobs move beyond challenging into the realm of being unfair. They have stuns, endless combos, ridiculous jumps, unblockable hits, and are so large and fast you cannot outrun them; nevermind the encounters in quests or dungeons which occur in cramped quarters where you have to master combat to have a chance. You may like to master combat, but the truth is there is luck involved in many of the boss fights, and not everyone likes the combat as much as the exploration or other things. 5. There is no quest journal to track steps completed, or even repeat goals or remind you of NPC names, or locations where you found them. That isn't just not holding your hand, that is stupid and not respecting your time. 6. The story really isn't very good at all. I understand that is subjective, but many players couldn't tell you the story if you asked them, unless they had read it from a third party site. Even if you do know it, it is boring, and RPGs are supposed to be story-driven, so a weak or non-compelling story-line is a problem. 7. You will experience burnout if you are like many others who have stated they eventually just skip fights and run straight through zones in the endgame, just wanting to say they completed the game, and for it to be over. In fact, I've read that many, myself included, have decided to not complete the game because it has become a chore. 8. There are hidden features like using gestures to unlock hidden areas supposedly. Well, you first have to find the gestures, then find the areas to use them, and then figure out which one to use. I would normally like such a feature, but I find it annoying in this game. If you try the game you will see what I mean. 9. The game implements soft caps on stats to force you to diversify your build and try different things. Look, if I want to max a stat and use the same weapon the whole game, then that is my business. Stop artificially forcing me to try play-styles I don't like. There is more to say, but there isn't much point when a game is so highly rated. The game has real issues for certain gamers that will continue to be dismissed by the fans who say that I need to get better at the game. But you see, I don't WANT to get better. I just want to enjoy the Elden Ring world using MY playstyle, not yours. This is one of the only developers that has decided they absolutely will not do that; it is their MO. I am all about developers deciding what type of game they want to make, and sticking to it. Elden Ring does that and I say good for them, but the result is a gamer like me is eventually driven away. Fans of this series are happy about that, because they are so scared the things they like will be changed, or that their bragging rights will become meaningless as more people can kill the bosses they do, but I think this is silly. There is some multiplayer functionality, but in the end this is a single player RPG and one gamer's sense of accomplishment shouldn't hinge on another gamer being shutout of the experience of the game to protect fragile egos and placate irrational fears. Let as many people as possible experience and enjoy the fantasy world created I say. For the reasons just stated, the game is so hyped that I believe the reviews never give you a fair assessment of the negatives, or at least the full picture. This game isn't just "not for everyone because it's hard." This game isn't for everyone because it has problems like any other. It doesn't have the best boss fights that exist, even if that is your thing. It is a challenge, and it is well done, but there is a HUGE segment of gamers that are also wasting their time with this game because it makes ZERO allowances for them in the end. I find myself wanting to explore every nook and cranny because the world is that good, but I cannot stand the stupid boss fights and respawning of mobs anymore. It has become tiring. I cannot stand that I can't turn the difficulty down if I want to. I cannot stand that the game is designed to make you repeat stuff because it wants you to die to experience a sense of accomplishment. Hey, if that's you then great, but it isn't me, and this game doesn't take a player like me into account. I wish it did.

In short, I feel like FromSoftware took all the aspects we liked from previous Soulsborne games and crafted this beautiful open-world RPG with it. It is a wonderful introduction to the genre of "souls-like." [b]Things I Liked:[/b] - The "play at your own pace" world structure. You aren't limited to a linear progression, so if you want to get stronger or explore other areas, you are able to do so. You don't have to fight main bosses with just what you gather in the starting area. In fact, if you don't care about 100%ing the game, you can completely skip some areas you don't like (looking at you, [spoiler]Caelid[/spoiler].) - More Grace Sites (bonfires)! I know in previous Soulsborne games, part of the challenge of the game was the fact that bonfires were spread out so much. But in Elden Ring, I don't think having so many Graces significantly lowers this challenge. Considering that Elden Ring is open-world, the amount of Grace Sites feels appropriate, and I think less would actually hurt the game. - The many different endings. Each ending [spoiler]significantly alters the world of Elden Ring[/spoiler] and there is no obvious "good" or "bad" ending. So this aspect combined with the many different classes/builds you can do makes every playthrough of Elden Ring unique and fun. - The spirit summons (also in the section below). Spirit summons help you feel not so alone when you're fighting bosses and can be really helpful in splitting agro. I especially thought [spoiler]the Mimic Tear[/spoiler] was a really cool experience and idea. [b]Things I Didn't Like:[/b] - The spirit summon reliance. Spirit summons are a really, REALLY useful tool against bosses. To the point that some bosses can be trivialized with them. You can fight bosses without them, but you almost feel like you have to use them, since it seems like some of the bosses are built with the usage of spirit summons in mind. What I'm trying to say is: I think the bosses would be more challenging and satisfying to kill if spirit summons weren't so OP. - The multi-boss fights. Specifically, [spoiler]the Godskin Duo[/spoiler]. Nasu put it well: in previous Soulsborne games, when you would encounter a multi-boss fight, one would usually take a more "passive" stance when the other is in a more "active" stance. This was a good balance. But in Elden Ring, they are usually both in a hyper-aggressive active stance which can definitely be frustrating to deal with. - You can't revisit [spoiler]Leyndell Royal Capital[/spoiler] after you [spoiler]defeat Maliketh[/spoiler]. This makes sense lore-wise, but it is frustrating if you're playing Elden Ring blind or simply didn't realize you didn't explore that area enough until it's too late. A fix perhaps would be to have a feature in the Roundtable Hold where you can toggle which version of [spoiler]Leyndell[/spoiler] you want access to after you beat the game. Overall, I can see why Elden Ring gained so much popularity, including from those where this was their first souls-like game. Its Game of the Year title was well-deserved. I highly suggest playing it if you haven't already.

Elden Ring is a masterpiece, having mastered the art of showing without telling. As a result, it is very different from other open-world games I have played such as Skyrim and Far Cry which are story and questline driven. From the get-go, Elden Ring doesn't impose any particular playstyle or route on you. You are completely free to do what you want to from the very start of the game. You can finish the main storyline and beat the final boss or you can explore the entire map without ever seeing the main bosses, it truly is up to you with no outside influence. It is truly refreshing to feel this sense of freedom in choice and exploration in any open world game. Elden Ring has also mastered the art of sublety. For example, for a game like Skyrim, there are various elements such as the character dialogues, leveling system, various landmarks that I could clearly point to in contributing to the game's success. However, this is not the same with Elden Ring. It's hard to place my finger on one specific thing that makes the game so enjoyable. Many times I've gone in to play this game for half an hour, only to become immersed, losing track of time and playing for hours on end. I belive that it's each of the game's features: its combat system, transportation, landscape, lore, storytelling, etc. that complement each other in a way that none of them are overbearing and at the same time, come together in such a fluid manner that I as the player can't notice it and am drawn into a level of immersion that I haven't felt from any game before. Other, more objective factors of Elden Ring are equally as impressive--it's hard to believe this is a $60 game. The map is massive, far bigger than I could've ever imagined, with more content packed into it than any other world game I've played before. I have not had a single moment where I've felt the map felt desolate or empty, there was always something to see and explore. The combat system is rich, balanced, and rewards each playstyle. The difficulty of the game is refreshing and I feel that I'm being challenged to improve and innovate as I play the game instead of relying on old hacks. The subtle details, such as changes in behavior over time of day or cross-NPC interactions add a layer of immersion that makes the world feel alive. It is also a very polished product: while games today are released with game-breaking bugs and issues, I haven't encountered a single bug in Elden Ring even given its massive map aside from minor visual glitches. It is truly astounding how much that adds to the immersion of the game. Overall, I feel that Elden Ring is an amazing game. While it isn't perfect by any means, in fact, the imperfections of the game give me something to look forward to for what will be the sequel to this, it will be hard to find a game from the last decade that is as immersive as this. I am truly impressed by From Software's work and I look forward to their next game. Elden Ring will inspire the next generation's set of games and I hope to see what comes from this. I've thoroughly enjoyed playing Elden Ring and I hope to see you too enjoy it.

[h1] The GOTY. The GOAT. [/h1] [b]The positives[/b] An absolute masterpiece by fromsoft, there is no way to meme around it. This game builds upon everything Demon souls, DS 1 - 3 and other games have done and turns it up to 11. build variety, weapons, spells, incantations, all have been massively improved (so miracle builds are actually viable for once) to the point I cant think of any build in elden ring that ISNT viable. all mainline bosses are amazing and most side bosses whilst reused a lot are also fun to fight. The story like other games is cryptic and the lore is hidden so using a wiki is recommended if you want to understand everything. NPCs are varied and amazing (ranni being my number 1 stunnagirl). Summons are varied and fun (black knife tiche, mimic tear, cleanrot knight, etc.) [hr][/hr] [b]Downsides[/b] However, on the downside the reuse of bosses around the map is VERY noticeable you'll find the tree sentinel in your bed at night, the crucible knight will shower with you. Its not as bad as it seems given they're usually fun to fight but It puts off exploration a lot when you know the boss is going to be a random field enemy but with 2x the health and 3x the damage. On top of this the difficulty spike going into late game areas is very noticeable and it gives you a lingering thought that leyndell was meant to be longer or harder. Bosses can be extremely easy and a lot of them have various cheeses (looking at you draconic tree sentinel) that takes the fun out of fighting them if you use them. Not to mention bleed is very heavily overused with other status effects being left in the dust (they did madness, death blight and sleep dirty). There are currently 3 endings. Lord ending, frenzied flame, and the age of stars. the others are all reskins of the lord ending with various outcomes. Melina is never used to her full potential aside from turning into bbq meat near the end or popping up in a cryptic cutscene and I never found myself truly caring for her from start to finish, I truly think they should've done more to tug at our heart strings to make Melina's death feel much more impactful. [hr][/hr] In conclusion the game is amazing even with its myriad of issues, and Id recommend anyone even souls newbies in giving it a shot. Video review: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MWIkdB7Gn8E ELDEN RING is what I always hoped and dreamed modern gaming would become. I am a huge DARK SOULS franchise fan and I would also declare this one easily the objective best one yet through the sheer hours of content at your fingertips. You are tarnished. A forgotten and unimportant soul who is maidenless. Luckily you meet Melina who is willing to guide you through your journey as your personal maiden / waifu. She gives you the reins to a spiritual beast named Torrent and your objective it to defeat the Shardbearers and ultimately become Elden Lord through one of the various ways of doing so. ELDEN RING is insane because it's a 2022 released game that is superior to all of it's predecessors and does not feature any kind of cheapness or monetization whatsoever. It's really a breath of fresh air and every waking moment spent playing this game is true peak escapism and entertainment factor. Featuring beautiful visuals and a way larger than necessary / expected world to explore. I've always liked the SOULS franchises' NPCs but this game takes it a step further in elaborating and explaining each and every character not to mention how cool they look and how they all stand out from each other. The bosses are the reason to play these games and whether FromSoftware realised that or just decided to go with an open world filled with seemingly endless bosses isn't actually important. The fact the player has a map, a steed, and fast travel from the get go between Sites of Grace make the quality of life so good for veterans of the series who just want to ride past everything, enjoy the scenery, and defeat some legendarily high quality bosses. Many people claim this is the easiest SOULS game but they are definitely wrong since there are some bosses in this game that are far more difficult than anything we've ever previously encountered; the hardest bosses from past games were Orphan of Kos & Darkeater Midir, and those two do not even compare to the likes of someone like Malenia, Blade of Miquella in this game who is borderline impossible to do solo no matter how good you are. The world and it's levels are obviously easier then past games and I prefer it this way actually; because it rewards thorough exploration and gives the player the ability to choose how much of a challenge they actually want since they can seek out more powerful weapons and Ashes if they want, and get early upgrade materials that will out-scale the majority of the game, or you can simply follow the linear path and go from story required boss to story required boss in a straight line without enhancing your character too much which will prove much more challenging. ELDEN RING is a one of a kind game and shows us how far FromSoftware has come from the cash grabby low effort days of something like DARK SOULS II. There will be nothing like this ever again I assume and if you only play one video game for the rest of your life, choose this one. 10/10.

I’ll be honest… I almost let negativity bias affect my outlook on this game. I -really- had to sit on my experience for a bit as to not let my burning problems with the game affect my full outlook on Elden Ring. Do I recommend it? Yes, but with some caution. There are parts that I loved and parts that were absolutely asinine for me to get through. The biggest positives extend to Exploration, world design and the build variety. Exploring the world is an absolute treat. There’s so much to see in the lands between and you’re basically just… let loose with enough direction to not feel aimless. This allows you to experience the world in a way that is completely unique to you. It is so special to experience on a first playthrough. And even when I restarted the game to give it a second chance (I abandoned my first playthrough after getting frustrated) I still had a great time exploring the world all over again. Every structure you see is something you can travel through and explore and it’s super rewarding to see a massive mansion in the distance. Travel over to it and explore every nook and cranny. Of course Elden Ring didn’t invent this or anything, but it’s been refined really well in my opinion. The world design as a whole is mysterious and alluring. You want to know what lies around every corner and what the meaning of all the bizarre and fantastic things you see. The world building through Item descriptions and NPC dialog gives you insight into the world, enough to know what you’re doing. But still leaves you asking and guessing. I loved the amount of choices you are given to build your character in this one. You can do things like Tanky strength builds using Hammers and Greatswords or Quick and flashy Dex builds using Katanas and Twinblades. Combine that with the spells and incantations you get throughout the game and you get even more options. You can dedicate yourself to being a spellcaster or go hybrid with some melee options. Within the Spells and incantations there are subclasses of spells and weapons and talismans to go with them. This in tandem with the Weapon arts and ashes of war create a wonderful variety of options to pick from. The best part about all this customization is the fact that you’re able to change a lot of this stuff with general ease. So if you’re not having fun with your current build. You can try something else. The build variety is something that I’m excited to try again if I ever come back to this one. But ultimately this game has a -few- big problems with it. And my 2 biggest problems with this game are the bosses and the endgame content (Which I won’t spoil it but I will warn of it) The smaller bosses are constantly reused and overdone. They’re only really appealing to fight 1-2 times which would be fine if you only fought them sparingly. Unfortunately the minibosses you fight get reused a lot. And it gets really old, really quick. The only way they up the difficulty in reused minibosses on repeat encounters is to add another copy of the boss or add a different miniboss that doesn’t compliment the first one. Leading to lazy reuses of bosses that just serve to pad out playtime and end dungeons. They also try to spice up boss rematches by doing duo bosses but they never really work. Because the boss movesets just don’t work together in tandem because they weren't created to work together. Literally any time they tried to do a duo boss it just fails. It’s either uncoordinated and messy but functional. Or just straight up unfun and frustrating. Not to mention that certain Miniboss enemies, some of which are treated in the similar breaths to the larger encounters in the game. Can just be found in the wild just hanging around the world for no reason… But then there’s the bigger bosses and it felt like Fromsoft went with a different approach when designing them. While I’m personally not huge on it I can see what they were going for. The bosses felt more like they were visual spectacles first and how much fun those -spectacles- end up actually being to fight come second. All the bosses look, sound, and act cool and they’re fun to fight when you’re watching somebody else do it. But when you’re experiencing some of these fights yourself the -spectacle- of them wear off real quick and the wow is quickly replaced by frustration… While the other souls games were “hard but fair” this game feels “frustrating but fair”. Sure I can dodge the mountains of bs being thrown my way but… trying to overcome these bosses feels frustrating. Sometimes I found myself wondering if some of these fights were tested to see if they were enjoyable to play instead of just “cool to look at”. What ended up happening was a minority of the fights were affecting my outlook on the larger picture. (IE: Malenia, Elden Beast, Fire Giant, Rykard) Because not all bosses are bad and unfun. Some are actually incredibly enjoyable and epic. But all of the bosses one way or another fell into one or more really annoying design pitfalls like attacks that are delayed unnaturally long, grab attacks that deal way too much damage and are way too punishing, super long combos which don’t give the player a chance to attack, and a camera that is zoomed in too close to see large enemies. Overall the bosses were the weakest part of the game and -really- hinders the replay value. Because I don’t want to redo some of these fights. Once was enough. Elden Ring’s endgame was easily the weakest part of it. Not only do the bosses get more frustrating than they were before. Not really pacing you with them and instead just, getting more unfair as you progress. The areas you explore get less open and more linear leading to a less rewarding experience. And the poor endgame (and one of the worst final bosses I’ve ever experienced in a video game) almost ruined my outlook of the game as a whole. Because it left a poor taste in my mouth walking away from the experience. But TLDR Do I recommend Elden Ring? If you love exploring and find bosses to be secondary in your enjoyment of a game. Then I can easily recommend this one. But if you’re like me and bosses are the highlights of action games like this. Elden Ring might leave you more frustrated than satisfied. And even with certain bosses (like the final one my god why did it have to incorporate every single problem with this game’s boss design) hurting my outlook when I was walking away from it. I still found Elden Ring to be a great game. Does it have flaws? Sure but those flaws didn’t ruin the game. Would I go back to it? Given some time (and maybe DLC) I could see myself coming back and maybe just skipping the parts I didn’t enjoy so much. But overall I could see myself recommending this one. But if you have any hangups about the difficulty… Maybe skip this one. The frustration you will experience might not be worth the positives. 4/5 Great. But not perfect.

Allora, questa recensione farà piangere i cringioni fanboy ma infondo ci sono abituato. Da dove iniziare? Partiamo dal presupposto che non siamo di fronte ad un titolo divertente. Un souls-like casa From divertente? Comprensibile come domanda, ma lasciatemi spiegare: Avendo completato chissà quante volte ormai tutta la trilogia souls, mai mi sono [/i]stancato[/i] di giocarci mid run. Certo, ci sono stati momenti di rage dovuti più che altro ad uno sviluppo fatto con il culo ma infondo pochi giochi posso vantare di essere veramente perfetti. Dunque il problema si pone qui, l'averlo abbandonato svariate volte perché non mi stava invogliando a farlo è un bel problema, dovuta alla mancanza di un vero obbiettivo; "gne gne aiuta la frignona melinda a bruciare l'anello così salvi il mondo" (Mi ricorda l'avventura di un gruppo di gnappette ma ok). No, darmi una mappa grossa come il Texas, piena di briciole di patatine con un'obbiettivo così generico e vago è una combo disastrosa. Per fortuna si sono accorti che un solo finale misero come quello sarebbe stato un suicidio, così si sono messi d'accordo per farne altri e almeno Ranni risolleva un minimo la trama; sarà perché puoi interagirci, sarà perché non è criptica ma ti da delle istruzioni precise, sarà che interagirai con altri personaggi a lei legati fanno si che sia l'unico finale degno di nota. Ora. Non che nei souls ci fosse chissà quale interazione con gli npc o una trama sfonda cervelli, ma almeno li non dovevi andare a tentoni raccogliendo briciole per capire che [/strike]minchia[/strike] fare e sopratutto dove andare. "Uhe Uhee ci sono i falò che nella mappa ti indicano dove andare Uhee", certo, una linea gialla che indica approssivamente 300 Km cubici di mappa inesplorata con all'interno 20 falò e solo uno che indica quello successivo. Difatti il problema più grande è appunto l'eccessiva ampiezza di una mappa priva di unicità, che per renderla dinamica, hanno spammato le stesse cose da fare, semplicemente aumentando la vita dei nemici presenti. Mettermi 236 (stando alla wiki) boss non rende il gioco più bello, sopratutto se metà di questi si riciclano a vicenda, ma solamente una completition list noiosa e sopratutto toglie quel senso di pericolosità e fierezza che avevano i boss. Ormai tutto è un boss, al punto che alla fine molti di essi li ritrovi come nemici da due soldi in qualche zona più avanti. Di conseguenza, trama banale e vaga, mappa eccessivamente grossa e priva di contenuto unico, stragrande maggioranza di boss senza una caratterizzazione e solo due elementi che si salvano: Scenari effettivamente belli, certe angolazioni del fiume Siofra sono incredibili e un gameplay fluido, ma grazie al [/strike]cazzo[/strike] è un copia e incolla di DS3 quindi funziona per forza. Quindi in definiva, dare una sufficienza a questo titolo è impossibile, game of the year rubato aggiungerei, per un titolo che è solamente un souls open world vuoto e senz'anima, che cerca di ricalcare i passi dei suoi predecessori, aggiungendo novità ma in malo modo. This is the culmination of all the previous Souls titles, into one gigantic game that seems to have somehow fit the same amount of content and detail of previous titles into a game multiple times larger than them. there are hundreds of weapons, spells, armor sets, weapon arts and they all come together to offer more variety in builds and play styles than any other Fromsoft game. However, this is not without a few faults that this game has that cannot be overlooked. Because this game is gigantic, shortcuts had to be made when it comes to content like bosses and mini dungeons, so reused bosses and environments can be found. This can cause issues with the lore and immersion, as sometimes a boss can be found in an cave that doesn't make sense wielding a weapon it usually shouldn't. While previous titles had a couple re used bosses, such as dragonslayer armor, guardian ape, or the cleric beast, in Elden Ring, there are actually only a few bosses that are not re used. This can take away from the suspense of fighting some of the better bosses, such as Godfrey and Mohg, since you already had experience with another version before their real fight. The other flaw is the very strange variance in difficulty, especially in the late game. World enemies become harder than bosses, with gigantic health pools and often are in large groups, like the zamor warriors in the mountaintops or the banished knights in castle sol. This combined with the lack of meaningful rewards from these enemies can mean the best course will be simply running past them, which is not an ideal strategy in a game centered around combat. This is offset by the endgame boss guantlet, which is one of the best I've ever seen. All in all, while I highly, highly, highly recommend this game, I do not recommend it as your first fromsoft game. Dark Souls 3 is much more streamlined in its difficulty and is much more straightforward and easy to approach, as opposed to the sheer scale of Elden Ring which might scare some people away. If you do want to push through and go into this game as your first, my best advice is to not give up and keep trying. If you're stuck at a boss or section, don't tunnel vision on that and instead go someplace else and check it out, find your own path that matches the difficulty experience you want, rather than what others may tell you to take.

Elden Ring is an action role playing RPG game/PP crusher simulator created by FromSoftware where you explore the open world of the Lands Between and fight hard bosses in between completing quests and trying not to die. I fell in love with the Soulsborne series when I first started playing Bloodborne on the PS4, after which I went out on a whim and bought myself Demon's Souls for PS3 as well as Dark Souls 1-3. I heard about this game a while ago, got hyped and pre-ordered as soon as I could before waiting a year to start the game. Having platinumed the game on PS5 and hoping to start on Steam someday in the future, here are my thoughts: The Story is one of those things that you just have to kind of explore and figure out by piecing together pieces of dialogue, item descriptions as well as environmental cues. I can't even tell you much of anything about it, but what I can say is like all FromSoft Souls titles, I love it. It keeps the goal simple: You're a Tarnished (an individual who was banned by the former queen from the Lands Between) who is going for the spot of Elden Lord and to do so has to fight through several different demigods in order to do so. You'll run into several characters via out in the world or the Hubworld, Roundtable Hold, who could do anything from basically nothing to giving you entire new endings. That's all I have to say for the plot: The Gameplay is basically almost the same as the other games in the Souls Series. You go from area to area to loot objects, fight bosses, complete particular quest lines for certain rewards, invade/fight enemy invaders except one caveat: It’s open world. And I mean it’s OPEN world. The other games were a lot more simplified as well as complex: they were a bit open in terms of pathways, shortcuts etc but they also had a straight way from point A to point B as well. In this game, everything is basically tenfold in terms of it’s game play design from how you get to certain areas to how to fight certain bosses. One example: [Spoiler] In order to get to Leyendell there’s a couple different ways you can get to that region. One is you could ride up the Grand Lift of Dectus, where you need two halves of a medallion in which you can get each at Forth Haight and Fort Faroth. Another way you could do it is by going underneath a church near the Lift, going through a village and climbing up a mountain before killing the Magma Wyrm and getting up that way. ANOTHER way is to get killed/abducted at the bottom of the waterwheel in Raya Lucaria where you wake up in an area at Volcano Manor and fight your way out of the caves.[/Spoiler] Stuff like this is mindblowing and is amazing how much attention to detail and scope it took to truly create such a thing. And keep in mind this is only one example, I can’t list everything because truthfully, like this game, there’s so much stuff TO list that I’d be making a f u c king video essay on it. But also in essence I do think that can be to this game’s detriment as well: It’s so huge that it’s kind of overwhelming with its scale, and with that it can lose some of it’s uniqueness when you see multiple of the same bosses repeated over and over again with different skins. I’ve always been someone who liked to coop anyways so I’ve been cool with it but it can be kind of frustrating at times with certain bosses. I guess to finish this off just be aware that this game is difficult yes, but the community is great. Sure, are there a s sholes who will just tell you to “Get Gud'' and make believe they aren’t a bunch of basement dwelling pee larpers? Yes. Sound Design/Art/Graphics; all of this is great and I’m not even sure I could expand upon it other than I don’t feel that the Soundtrack is as memorable as the other souls games? Still it looks great, the art design is amazing and graphics are good too. I can’t do justice to this game in a single Steam review, but if you’re new to the series or you wanna try it out just know this: Play fresh, wing it a bit and have fun, try not to get overwhelmed and experience EVERYTHING because it’s impossible (though it is possible to get all the trophies in one playthrough if that’s your thing). Research the game a bit, see what builds you want to go for (though your starting class does kind of gear you in certain ways so I’d say research BEFORE you start the game unless you just kinda want to wing it), farm a bit and upgrade your stats. But please god take breaks and take it at your own pace; because you will die and die and die some more and then die again; it can be a frustrating and strange loop but when it clicks with you it clicks with you. Given all the hype this game received, well, eventually I should probably learn to not trust "professional" game reviewers. I'm not sure if this is the studio's first open world game, but it sure feels like it. It's a bland and boring (but beautiful) world with no direction and incredibly repetitive mechanics that become boring after the second dungeon you go through. You don’t need direction in a linear game like dark souls (rather, its linear nature IS the direction). But open world games need at least some of it. Given all the hidden secrets in this world, I can tell just how much effort the devs put into crafting it. But with how they just point you in a vague direction and say “go kill that boss to advance!”, they utterly fail their lovingly crated world by not giving the user any real reason to explore it. I saw a lot of reviewers saying that you should use a notepad with this game to keep track of side quests because there is not quest log. If your players are having to use external tools to keep track of something in the game, that’s a failing on the game’s part. It does not add to the experience or mystique of the game. In fact, it detracts, since you have to consciously put the game aside to take notes. I didn’t get far enough into the game to really judge how much you’d have to use the wiki to find secrets and solve puzzles, but if what little I did get is an indication of the rest of the game, then another symptom of the lack of direction is just how often people have to search online to figure out how to find something or what to do next. Again, if your players are have to use external tools to play the game, it’s a failing of the game. I've yet to find any appreciable story after 15 hours of play. And no, a few lines of dialogue every now and then are NOT story. They're a pathetic attempt to pretend to have a story. Maybe if I played longer, I'd see more interesting content and more story, but if I'm not seeing any real story even after I down the first major boss, I do not count that as having a story. It's flavor text, at most. As a final note on the negatives: This is a lazy console port. Framerate is capped at 60, Field of View is too narrow for computer screens, and not adjustable. Interface is taken directly from the console, and that's almost never a good thing for a PC game. Control scheme has terrible pre-bound keys, and commands that should really be split between multiple keys on a PC are bound together. Additionally, there are a number of commands that can not be re-bound. Number keys can not be bound to any commands. And there's probably more that I'm forgetting about. This game is playable with a kb/mouse, would probably be better with a controller, but REALLY needed a interface/control rework for PC. As for the last part, let me preface this by saying it does NOT factor into my negative review, because I know many people very much so enjoy the souls-like model. This was my first souls like game, and it turns out I do NOT enjoy the punishing mechanics that you have to corpse drag through to learn fights. I get that others do, and I won't review it negatively because of that. Though piece of advice, if you think you won't like the punishing challenge of the souls-like model, do not buy a souls-like game, you'll just be miserable. If you don't have really good reactions, you won't be able to handle combat in this game. People say git gud, and that's the kind of game this is. I just have no interest and do not enjoy it. Again, this is not why I'm giving the game a negative review, just a warning to anyone who might be looking to try the souls like model.
